But you never caught it. It caught you. You may not have known what was happening at first, but you're well aware now. That when night comes, you stop being yourself.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: That's insane.
entries.speaker: Dr. Ian Detweiler

entries.text: You become the trickster. A shape-shifting man who becomes an animal.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: I've heard enough.
entries.speaker: Dr. Ian Detweiler

entries.text: No. You killed because you could. You may have resisted it at first. You may have hated what you'd become. Eventually it took you over. That's where the tranquilizer came in. I found traces of etorphine in animal blood at the clinic. You injected yourself with a tranquilizer hoping to stop the killings. But they didn't and they haven't and they won't.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: [ quiet chattering ]
entries.speaker: Sound

entries.text: I protected you as long as I could. I won't any longer.
entries.speaker: Karin Berquist

entries.text: I can usually get a sense of a person right away from the dogs. Dogs are the best judges of character I know.
entries.speaker: Karin Berquist

entries.text: I'm sensing something myself here. I'm thinking maybe I've been misled. That you haven't been totally honest with me about this case.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: I've been honest with you, though perhaps not myself. I was looking forward to meeting you. I wouldn't admit how much.
entries.speaker: Karin Berquist

entries.text: But you might also have admitted what you knew about this animal, that it wasn't an animal at all.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: I heard the reports and called you out, if only so you could disprove them. What I knew was it couldn't be a dog responsible for those killings.
entries.speaker: Karin Berquist

entries.text: It's Detweiler, isn't it?
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: Yes.
entries.speaker: Karin Berquist

entries.text: So you knew that and didn't say?
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: I only realized it when I saw him. My failure was in thinking I was protecting the animal. That by deceiving you, it might be captured alive. He's got to be put down, Fox. It's the only way to stop this.
entries.speaker: Karin Berquist

entries.text: Well, I've got Scully on him, tailing him, watching his every move.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: He'll elude her easily.
entries.speaker: Karin Berquist

entries.text: But where's he gonna go?
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: To the man he only wounded. To the hospital to finish the kill.
entries.speaker: Karin Berquist

entries.text: [ dialing phone ]
entries.speaker: Sound

entries.text: Scully, it's me. You gotta get to the hospital. You gotta make sure Cahn is protected. Yeah, he's in danger.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: Want to tell me why you pulled me away from the suspect and chained me to this chair? 'cause I haven't seen hide nor hair of Detweiler since I've been here.
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: That's aptly put. It's not yet dark. You should take a load off. We might be here all night.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: What do you mean?
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: It's Detweiler. It's not Detweiler, it's something he becomes.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: Mulder.
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: Through some blood curse, this man undergoes some kind of nocturnal transformation. He becomes the same shape-shifting trickster as that mythical dog.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: So is he gonna walk in here, skitter across the linoleum and pee in the corners?
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: It's about territoriality. He's gonna come back here tonight to make sure his dominance isn't challenged. He's gonna put down the threat he failed to eliminate when he attacked Cahn. Karin Berquist confirmed it.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: Mulder, the only thing Karin Berquist is interested in is you. You're kidding yourself... If you think that she hasn't manipulated this entire situation... For her own purposes.
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: He'll come here tonight, Scully. You'll see.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: [ dogs whimpering ]
entries.speaker: Sound

entries.text: Okay. He's not comin'.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: [ sighs ] well, you've got no argument from me.
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: He's not comin' here tonight. Karin knew that. She lied to me.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: [ phone ringing ] [ gasps ]
entries.speaker: Sound

entries.text: Karin, it's Fox Mulder. I know what you're doing. If you can hear me, lock your doors. I'm on my way.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.speaker: Sound

entries.text: Come on, dog.
entries.speaker: Karin Berquist

entries.text: [ snarling continues ]
entries.speaker: Sound

entries.text: Come on. Come on.
entries.speaker: Karin Berquist

entries.text: [ dogs barking ]
entries.speaker: Sound

entries.text: Mulder.
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: Yeah, it's Detweiler.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: You going home?
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: Yeah, pretty soon.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: You think this is your fault.
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: I think that I... Believed her very quickly. I think maybe that was my fault, yeah.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: Why wouldn't you believe her?
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: I barely knew her.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: Well, she had a lot of secrets, that's for sure. I think that Karin Berquist lived by her instincts. She sized people up pretty quickly, and I think she figured you out to a tee. I think she saw in you a kindred spirit, Mulder. She may not have been able to express that to you. Maybe what she did was the highest form of compliment.
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: [ sighs ]

entries.text: You gonna be okay? Oh, this came for you.
